kinds.d: Hops sold for brewing, as pellets or whole cones, by variety.

x.d: Czech noble hop named after Žatec; mild, earthy, herbal and spicy, the hop of Bohemian pilsner; Czech alpha 2.5-4.0%.
German hop from the Hallertau region of Bavaria, alpha about 3.5-5.5%.
English hop sold under that name since 1838; smooth, sweet bitterness with spicy, earthy aroma.
English Kent hop noticed growing wild in 1861 and commercialised in 1875; earthier and less sweet than Goldings.
American aroma hop from the USDA programme at Oregon State, bred 1956 and released 1971-72; floral, spicy and citrus with slight grapefruit.
American hop first crossed in 1990 and released in 2007; grapefruit and tropical fruit, alpha 11-13%.
American hop with tropical, blueberry, tangerine, floral and earthy notes; alpha 11.5-13.5%.
American hop released in 2000: passion fruit, pine, earthy and citrus, alpha 12-14%.
New Zealand hop developed in 1987 and sold since 2000, with a strong suggestion of passionfruit.
Australian hop bred in 1994 with citrus and passionfruit aroma.

kinds.d: Malted barley and other grains for mashing: base malts that convert their own starch and specialty malts for colour and flavour.

x.d: Two-row winter barley bred at the Plant Breeding Institute, Cambridge, introduced in 1966 and prized for real ale.
Spring two-row barley from gamma-irradiated Maythorpe, grown commercially in Scotland from 1967; Simpsons Malt secured its variety rights in 2015.
The lightest generally available base malt, with a sweet malt flavour, basis of pale lagers.
Slightly darker, hotter-kilned malt for Vienna lager and Märzen, usually 10-15% of the grist but able to serve as base.
Darker base malt for bocks with enough enzymes to self-convert; malty rather than sweet.
Specialty malt wetted and roasted in a drum, fully converted, adding toffee-like sweetness; contains no enzymes.
Specialty malt kilned hotter than amber malts, adding chocolate and cocoa flavour to porters and stouts; no enzymes.

kinds.d: Concentrated malt wort, liquid or dry, for brewing or baking.
Yeast for home brewing and winemaking.

x.d: Fermentis dry American ale yeast, widely sold to homebrewers in sachets and 500 g packs.
Family of Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains from western Norway that ferment up to 43 °C, finish fast and often give tropical-fruit aromas; sold by labs in several countries.

kinds.d: Ready-to-brew kits of malt extract, hops and yeast, from simple cans to all-grain sets.

x.d: Kits from Coopers of Adelaide, the world's largest producer of canned beer concentrate for homebrewing; brewery founded by Thomas Cooper in 1862.
Muntons' craft-style 35-pint kits of Hazy IPA, Milk Stout and West Coast IPA, launched in 2021.

kinds.d: Concentrated grape or apple juice kits for home wine and cider; grape concentrate bricks were once sold for this in Prohibition-era America.

brands.d: Adelaide brewery founded by Thomas Cooper in 1862; the world's largest producer of canned beer concentrate for homebrewing.
Stowmarket, Suffolk maltster making homebrew kits since the 1970s; Flagship range launched 2021.
Maltster that bought a farm in 1983 to keep Golden Promise barley in supply and acquired its variety rights in 2015.
Maker of SafAle dry brewing yeasts including US-05.
